examples.title: Bidirectional Bag binding
examples.description: Two client Bags share one server branch through dataBinder.
examples.explanation: Edit either quantity and leave the field. Both copies agree; the server controller calculates the total. Try a negative quantity to see a business error in Data.

examples.title: Publish a customer request
examples.description: Publish a key; a subscribed PageStore controller puts the record and outcome in its Bag.
examples.explanation: Load customer 1 or 2, then try 99. A missing customer preserves the previous record and key. The publication acknowledges acceptance; the binder carries the business outcome.

examples.title: Publish from a page family
examples.description: Direct and nested iframes and connected windows publish through the primary's single WebSocket.
examples.explanation: Load different customers in each frame or window. Each has its own PageStore. The gallery owns the connection; closing it closes connected descendant windows.

examples.title: Publish to another page
examples.description: A child window publishes to the PageStore of another page owned by the same owner.
examples.explanation: Copy the recipient's page ID into the connected sender window. The recipient's PageStore updates its Bag and publishes customer_loaded back to the sender, where a subscribed dataController displays the event separately from acceptance.
